evidenceClass: closed-form formula diagnostic plus exact finite lattice enumeration
analyticalQuestion: How does the high-frequency penalty change between direct H3 entry and critical homogeneous-H1/2 entry, and what can a linear heat-semigroup benchmark show without a nonlinear Duhamel estimate?
supportedTakeaway: After radius normalization, the sufficient frequency penalty improves from N^-3 to N^-1/2; for a_N=cN^-gamma, the open strip 1/2<gamma<3 has L2 and homogeneous H1/2 tending to zero while homogeneous H3 diverges. The heat-semigroup panel is linear only.
chartFamily: three-panel log-log comparison, exponent phase diagram, and discrete-envelope diagnostic

palettePolicy.policy: two chromatic roots with redundant non-color encoding

quantifiers.pureModeScaling: For every gamma in (1/2,3), every c>0, and every fixed critical radius R>0, there exists N0=N0(c,R,gamma) such that c*N^(1/2-gamma)<R for every integer N>=N0; simultaneously c*N^-gamma tends to zero and c*N^(3-gamma) tends to infinity.
quantifiers.endpointCaveat: At gamma=1/2, homogeneous H1/2 size is the prefactor c up to the fixed Fourier normalization and entry requires a strict prefactor inequality.
quantifiers.heatEnumeration: For every plotted tau in [0.001,10], exhaustive three-square enumeration through norm squared 4096 gives the global discrete lattice maximum because 4096>3/(2*0.001) and the radial objective decreases thereafter.
